caption:
This morning: a new benchmark shows sixteen AI agents succeed on 64 to 84 percent of strict CRM tasks. The gap between saying and doing is real.

Three more data points: grading only the reply overstates success by about 11 points. The earlier CRMArena-Pro saw multi-turn success fall to 35 percent. Zapier's strict AutomationBench tops out at 51.29 percent.

My take: a good reply proves very little. Measure what changed in the record, against your own rules.

Comment CPQ and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning: sixteen agents score 64 to 84 percent on strict CRM checks. I went back in to see what sits around that number.
First, grading only the reply overstates strict success by 10.5 to 11 points, according to the paper itself. Saying is not doing.
Second, on the earlier CRMArena-Pro, agents dropped from about 58 percent single-turn to 35 percent multi-turn, The Decoder reports.
Third, Zapier's AutomationBench also grades the end state strictly, and its top score is 51.29 percent.
My take: a chat reply proves little. Count what changed in the record, against your own rules, before you trust the agent.
